title: The superionic boundaries of water and ammonia: the pressure and temperature where each turns superionic, and where it melts to an ionic fluid (GEN.1422)

sources.water_floor: [R5181] (READ, arXiv text): bcc superionic ice appears from ice VII at 20 GPa and 900 K, and between 20 and 60 GPa the transformation is seen on heating to 900-1900 K; fcc superionic ice appears at 29 GPa and 1300 K and is the only phase above 60 GPa; [R3081] (abstract, READ): superionic ice XVIII at 100 to 400 GPa by shock compression. Above 60 GPa the floor is held at the 60 GPa value (STAND-IN SI1): no measured floor between 60 and 190 GPa was opened.
sources.water_ceiling: [R5181] (READ): water heated at 33 to 105 GPa is strongly absorptive (conducting fluid) above 4000 K and the fcc-SI melt line sits close to that at 105 GPa; partial melting at 5200 K and 150 GPa; a single shock-derived point near 5000 K at 190 GPa. The line from the 20 GPa, 900 K triple point to the 105 GPa, 4000 K point is an interpolation (STAND-IN SI2).
sources.water_metallic: [R5172] (abstract, READ): water turns metallic above 7000 K at 30 to 300 GPa.
sources.ammonia_floor: [R5172] (abstract, READ): ammonia has a superionic solid phase between the solid and the ionic liquid at 30 to 300 GPa and 300 to 7000 K. The onset of 60 GPa and 1500 K is RECALLED, not opened (STAND-IN SI3, Marginal educated guess from physics).
sources.ammonia_metallic: [R5172] (abstract, READ): ammonia turns metallic above 5500 K.
